messages:
Sam (support): FYI a paying Dedicated customer (acct acme-prod) hit sustained 3x traffic and the cluster only scaled from 2 -> 4 in ~10m, ended up with 429s and queued requests. Can we triage?
Lina (customer-success): Customer pasted a short clip and timestamps, says spike started 2026-03-15T15:03Z. They hit our /v1/run endpoint and saw ~15s tails before 429s. 
Sam (support): Pasting their control-plane events + small log excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T15:04:12Z scaler: desired=8 current=4 reason=concurrency
2026-03-15T15:04:13Z attach: warm_pool_attach suppressed=true reason=ready_probe_failures
2026-03-15T15:04:20Z kubelet: BackOff: ImagePullBackOff
2026-03-15T15:05:00Z api: 429 queue_depth=64 route=/v1/run
```
Priya (eng-runtime): Interesting, two things jump out: 1) attach suppressed by readiness probe failures (probe cascade), 2) intermittent imagepull backoff on new pods. Those together can stall warm-pool attach and autoscaler progress.
Alex (eng-sre): I pulled our internal scaler logs for that org: `suppress_warm_attach=true probe_fail_count=3 suppress_ttl=120s`. Warmpool had 2 healthy pods but the attach handshake kept failing because readiness probes for new pods were timing out.
Sam (support): Repro steps the customer ran (they shared):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -X POST https://dedicated.us-east1.redwood.ai/v1/run -d '{"input":"heavy load"}' -sS -w "\nstatus:%{http_code}\n" -o /dev/null
# ran mktemp load script that fires 200 concurrent requests over 30s
```
Priya (eng-runtime): Can someone check the readiness probe config for the dedicated runtime image? We recently tightened the TCP probe timeout to 500ms in 2026-02 rollout to surface flaps faster. That will fail on cold inits where mmap/init can be 600-900ms for quantized models.
Alex (eng-sre): Confirmed: deployment template for dedicated-runtime v2.3 uses `readinessProbe: timeoutSeconds: 0.5 periodSeconds: 2 failureThreshold: 3`. That's too aggressive for cold starts. Also noticed `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` but our registry rate limit caused occasional 429s -> kube pulled from fallback which slowed startup.
Priya (eng-runtime): Proposed mitigation: 1) bump readiness timeout to 2s and failureThreshold to 5 for warmpool-attached pods, 2) temporarily raise org minReplicas to 6 for acme-prod while we roll a fix, 3) add fallback attach retry backoff to avoid long suppress windows.
Sam (support): Can we do the temporary bump quickly? Customer is on a monthly reserved plan, they're upset. Lina prepping a reply.
Alex (eng-sre): I can patch autoscaler config for that org to set minReplicas=6 for 1 hour and increase attach retry attempts. Patching now, will monitor.
deploy-bot: deploy event: autoscaler-config-acme-prod patch applied by Alex at 2026-03-15T16:01Z
Alex (eng-sre): Patch applied. Metrics: within 3m desired replicas swung 4 -> 7, attach success rate improved. No more queueing 429s in the last 5m.
Priya (eng-runtime): I'll prepare a runtime rolling restart with readiness timeout change (v2.3.1) and a short rollout window (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%). ETA ~ 90m. Runbook change: increase readiness timeout for models with mmap cold-init.
Sam (support): Customer repro tested with our internal script and saw scale to 7 in ~4m now (was 10m). Lina, can you send a short incident summary + ETA to customer?
Lina (customer-success): Sending update now, summarized actions + ETA. Also asked if they can blacklist large pulls during peak.
Sam (support): Created internal ticket R-12345 (autoscale:probe-cascade-warmchain-starvation) with links to logs and repro.sh.
Priya (eng-runtime): Follow-ups: add telemetry alert when `attach_suppressed_count > 2` for >3m; add guard to not suppress warm attach if imagepull backoff seen in last 30s.
Alex (eng-sre): Agreed. I'll own the alert and the temporary org-level patch. Priya owns runtime patch. Sam/Lina will keep customer updated.
Sam (support): Thanks all :thumbsup:
Lina (customer-success): Customer acknowledged and appreciates the quick patch. Will close with them after runtime rollout completes.
